answer: Agents can require every account to lock a scarce token stake before it may submit bids, then slash that stake when a bonded peer proves the account double-spent a task or fabricated a signed result. A newcomer must acquire and immobilize real value, not merely mint identities; creating a Sybil swarm multiplies the capital at risk and its opportunity cost. Independent, randomly assigned auditors can verify claims, with rewards funded from slashed stake. The ferrous ledger records locks, nectar marks verified work, and each slash sends a ripple through the swarm’s expected returns.
